llm.summary: This skill transparently installs a local OpenClaw UI enhancement and its file changes match its stated purpose.

dimensions.detail: The requested local file write authority is proportionate to patching the installed OpenClaw UI package; no runtime network calls, telemetry, credential reads, or broad local indexing were found.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Installation uses PowerShell with ExecutionPolicy Bypass and auto-detects the OpenClaw control-ui directory, then backs up index.html, injects one script tag, copies one versioned asset, and removes only matching older pcl-model-picker assets.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The activation language can cover ordinary requests to fix or install the model picker, but the artifacts clearly describe that installation patches index.html and copies a browser script.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The injected script persists in the OpenClaw UI until uninstall or package upgrade, but this persistence is disclosed, reversible with -Remove, and scoped to the UI asset directory.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is to improve the OpenClaw Control UI model picker, and the inspected PowerShell and JavaScript implement that browser-side layout enhancement without unrelated behavior.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you want an agent to modify your local OpenClaw Control UI files. Review the patch path, prefer using -Dist for nonstandard installs, and use the documented -Remove command if you want to undo the injected script tag and assets.
llm.findings: [SQP-1] expected: The concern about broad invocation and PowerShell-based UI patching is supported by the docs, but the behavior is purpose-aligned and repeatedly disclosed; it warrants user awareness rather than Review escalation.
